### A half-written form can be corrected

The REPL reads a multi-line form as one editing session now.  Enter on an
unfinished expression opens the next line instead of submitting it, so the whole
expression stays in the buffer:

* **brackets match across the rows.**  A bracket opened on the first row and
  closed on the last is matched, and the closing bracket is no longer drawn as
  an error.  Colouring was done one row at a time, which meant neither row ever
  saw both ends of a pair;
* **backspace climbs.**  At the start of a continuation line it removes the line
  break and carries on into the line above, so a multi-line form can be edited
  back down to its first line rather than only abandoned with Ctrl-C.

Each row is drawn behind its own prompt — `>>> ` for the first, `... ` for the
rest — and the cursor is placed from that row's prompt, which is what keeps the
column right on every row.

### Compiled files are executable

`goscheme compile` writes a shebang and sets the execute bits:

```sh
goscheme compile prog.scm -o prog.scmc
./prog.scmc
```

The mode is added to whatever the file already had, matching read bits to
execute bits, rather than being set to a fixed value — compiling over a file
does not quietly change permissions you chose.  The reader skips the shebang, so
a file compiled by an older version — which has none — still reads.

### Cancellation costs nothing when it cannot happen

Running a file cannot be interrupted, so the machine no longer looks.  The check
in both engines is now a flag that is off unless the REPL is evaluating a form,
which is also faster than the channel test it replaces: measured pinned to a
core and repeated, the VM is 3.6% to 5.4% faster than before this release.
